1. The Scream

15×20 · 128 filled cells (43%) · dark-ink, threshold 102

Solvability: CLEAN — unique and fully logic-solvable, no hint cells needed.

Auto-removed singleton cells (1-based x,y; say the word to restore any): [[8, 3], [15, 3], [1, 13], [1, 20]]

Dark-ink polarity: the figure, the fjord's far shore, and the railing carry the fill; the sky and walkway stay empty. 4 stray single cells auto-removed.

DRAFT FACT

Munch said the vision behind The Scream came on a real sunset walk: the sky turned blood red and he felt 'an endless scream passing through nature.' He made four versions of it; two were stolen in armed heists and later recovered.

factSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Scream · attribution: Public domain

2. The Birth Of Venus

15×10 · 77 filled cells (51%) · light-ink, threshold 124

Solvability: CLEAN — unique and fully logic-solvable, no hint cells needed.

No singleton cells removed.

Light polarity: the PALE figures and the shell are the fill, so the painting's three-figure group is the shape. (Dark-mode framed them as negative space; this reads much more like the painting.)

DRAFT FACT

Botticelli painted The Birth of Venus around 1485, showing the goddess blown ashore by the wind gods. A large mythological nude was radical at the time, when nearly every major commission was religious.

factSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Birth_of_Venus · attribution: Public domain

3. Water Lilies

15×15 · 112 filled cells (50%) · light-ink, threshold 107

Solvability: CLEAN — unique and fully logic-solvable, no hint cells needed.

Auto-removed singleton cells (1-based x,y; say the word to restore any): [[14, 1], [3, 2], [2, 11]]

Light polarity: the fill is the pale sky-reflection on the water with the brightest pad clusters; the dark reflection masses read as shadow. Impressionist texture, like starry night's abstraction.

DRAFT FACT

Monet painted roughly 250 water lily canvases over his last three decades, all from the pond he designed and planted himself at Giverny. He worked on several at once, moving between easels as the light changed.

factSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Water_Lilies_(Monet_series) · attribution: Public domain

Solvability: CLEAN — unique and fully logic-solvable, no hint cells needed.

No singleton cells removed.

Light polarity: the fill is the lit diner interior and the sidewalk glow — the iconic part of the painting. ⚠ COPYRIGHT FLAG: painted 1942, so it is NOT public domain (the Excel's 'PD pre-1929' label is wrong); US copyright runs through 2037. The puzzle grid can ship, but the win-screen photo of the painting cannot. Options: (a) cut it, (b) keep the puzzle with a different win image, (c) defer the whole thing. Your ruling.

DRAFT FACT

Edward Hopper painted Nighthawks in 1942, inspired by a diner near his New York studio. The diner has no visible door to the street, which critics read as quiet isolation; Hopper said he was mostly painting the light.

factSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nighthawks_(painting) · attribution: ⚠ NOT public domain — see flag above
